characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure characterization; ferrite content and austenite grain size analysis

Intragranular κ-carbides dispersed in austenite after 723 K/3 h aging, coherent with austenite ([100]γ//[100]κ); submicron white particles identified as NbC.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Nano-scale κ-carbides could be sheared by dislocations under plastic deformation.
Large-size NbC particles are impermeable and their strengthening contribution is assessed by the Ashby-Orowan equation.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength (0.04Nb steels exceed 0.02Nb steels by ≈71 MPa, mainly due to additional fine grain strengthening and dislocation strengthening)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot prepared by induction melting in a water-cooled copper crucible; re-melted and swiftly poured into a rotating copper mold at high speed to obtain steel strips of 60×70×2.5 mm.

Aging treatment performed on a portion of the steel strips in a tubular vacuum furnace at 723 K for 3 h; 723 K was selected as the aging temperature giving better comprehensive mechanical properties for extended aging studies.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm
